Subject: ACME-RFP-892 - Private deployment operator handbook & transfer questions

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the quick onboarding window. ACME Health (RFP ACME-RFP-892) is evaluating private deployment options and we need a concise operator-facing handbook and clarifications on your airgapped image transfer process for procurement. A few concrete asks to help our security and procurement teams: 

1) Operator handbook: a short runbook that covers install, patching, operator roles and daily checks. Who is the primary operator persona and how many operator seats do you recommend for a 24/7 hospital environment?

2) Airgap / offline image transfer: we need the step-by-step for bringing model artifacts and runtime images into an isolated environment. Specifically: checksums, signing, offline verification tooling, and whether you support transfer via removable media vs. secure courier.

3) KMS/HSM: what integrations exist? Can keys be customer-managed and stored in an HSM behind our VPC?

4) Licensing & pricing ask: ballpark cost for a single dedicated VPC deployment (2x A100 equivalent) plus a one-time ops enablement fee; procurement timeline is targeting decision by 2026-06-03.

Please attach any operator checklist, the SLA template, and a sample playbook if available. We're happy to schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough; mornings (ET) this week work best for us.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morales
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Health
emorales@acmehealth.com

Subject: Re: ACME-RFP-892 - Private deployment operator handbook & transfer questions

Hi Elena — thanks for the detailed list and the timeline. We're excited to support ACME's evaluation. Quick answers and next steps below.

Short answers:
- Operator handbook: we have a targeted "Operator Checklist" (attached) that maps runbook tasks to personas (Operator, Platform Lead, Security Reviewer). Recommended seats: 2 primary operators + 1 escalation engineer for 24/7 coverage for your scale; we can adapt based on your runbook.
- Airgap transfer: we support signed artifact bundles with SHA-256 checksums, optional PKCS#7 signing, and an offline verification tool we provide as a signed binary. Transfers by removable media are supported; we also work with approved secure courier flows. Details in the attached playbook.
- KMS/HSM: customer-managed keys via your KMS are supported; we provide integration adapters for AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and on-prem PKCS#11 HSMs. Keys used for model encryption and operator credentials can be stored only in your KMS (no key material leaves your control).

Attachments I’m including: initial-operator-checklist.pdf (runbook summary), private-deploy-sla-template.pdf (SLA + support scopes), and the high-level airgap playbook stub. Irene will follow up with technical specifics and the signed binary details.

For pricing, Vanessa will loop in the pricing letter and estimates. Can we set a 30-minute walkthrough on Wed 05/20 at 10:00 AM ET? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite with a tech agenda.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: ACME-RFP-892 - Airgap image transfer & KMS details

Hi Elena,

Following Sofia's note — below is a concise technical summary of our airgap image and artifact transfer procedure plus KMS/HSM options. I'm flagging the items most often requested by GRC teams so you can drop them into the RFP response.

Airgap image transfer (typical flow):
1) Build & sign (Redwood internal): we produce a single artifact bundle (.tar.gz) containing runtime binaries, container images (tar snapshots), and model artifacts. Each file has a SHA-256 checksum and the bundle is signed using our build signing key (optional PKCS#7 envelope for customer verification).
2) Attestation report: a machine-readable attestation (JSON) with checksums, build IDs, and a timestamp is produced. We can provide a signed attestation or a human-readable manifest on request.
3) Offline distribution: the artifact bundle can be exported to removable media (FIPS 140-2/140-3 USBs recommended) or downloaded to a temporary staging host for courier pickup.
4) On-prem verification: customers run our offline verifier (signed binary) that verifies the PKCS#7 signature and compares SHA-256 checksums; verifier returns a signed success/failure report.
5) Key handling: model encryption keys are wrapped with a customer-managed KEK (Key Encryption Key) from your HSM/KMS. The unwrapped DEK (data encryption key) never leaves the airgapped environment in plaintext.

Operational notes & guardrails:
- Rollback & immutability: each bundle is immutable and stores a versioned manifest; operators should confirm checksum and attestation before update.
- Patch cadence: we recommend quarterly runtime patches and monthly critical security updates; emergency hotfix channel available with documented escalation.
- Operator personas: Operator (day-to-day), Platform Lead (deployment/rollbacks), Security Reviewer (attestation sign-off).
- Audit evidence: we can provide per-release signing logs, build provenance, and the verifier run logs as part of your evidence package.

Attachments attached: airgap-image-transfer-playbook.pdf (detailed steps), kms-integration-summary.docx (KMS/HSM adapters and API snippets).

If you'd like, I can include a sample verifier run output and a minimal checklist your SOC team can run during an update window.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

[Attachments: airgap-image-transfer-playbook.pdf, kms-integration-summary.docx]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: ACME-RFP-892 - artifact verification and model rollback notes

FYI — adding a couple of notes you can drop into the runbook/attestation section:

- Artifact checksums: we use SHA-256 by default and include an optional SHA3-512 field for customers that require stronger hashing.
- Model artifact fingerprints: each model includes a content-addressable manifest and a provenance header with training checksum and quantization profile.
- Rollback window: recommend a 72-hour operational rollback window where operator-approved rollbacks are allowed; after that, full reconciliation is triggered.
- Quantized model compatibility: when we ship int8 quantized variants, we include a compatibility matrix and a small runtime validator that sanity-checks tokenization and top-k distributions post-deploy.

Happy to draft a short paragraph for the runbook if Irene wants to include it.

Rishi
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
